principles: Narrow lifecycle artifact allowlist only; never blanket-allow .koala or evidence directories.
TEST-generated delivery evidence should be classified by provenance, not treated as product implementation drift.
Gate receipts and scope classification remain separate: allowing a file path does not satisfy delivery-check.
Regression tests must prove both the allowed transcript path and the adversarial rejected paths.
drivers: B-bffc caused real TEST to DEV churn solely due to required transcript evidence.
scope_contract_acknowledge is intentionally forbidden in TEST, so TEST generated evidence needs classifier support.
The safety boundary depends on rejecting arbitrary story metadata and product source paths.

options.name: narrow-transcript-lifecycle-artifact
pros: Fixes the observed B-bffc friction directly.
Keeps product source scope enforcement unchanged.
Does not alter reviewer or delivery-check gates.
cons: Only covers transcript-diff.md; future delivery evidence filenames need explicit registration.

options.name: allow-all-story-evidence-directory
pros: Avoids future work for new evidence files.
cons: Too broad; arbitrary evidence files could bypass scope review.
Conflicts with the lifecycle artifact policy closed-set intent.

options.name: allow-scope-acknowledge-in-TEST
cons: Works around the wrong layer and reintroduces TEST to DEV style churn.
Contradicts documented policy that TEST generated artifacts should be handled by classifier, not acknowledgement.

rationale: Choose the narrow transcript lifecycle artifact classification because it fixes the exact user-facing friction without weakening scope, review, or delivery gates.

preMortem.trigger: Implementation checks only path prefix instead of closed relative path.
preMortem.consequence: Out-of-scope metadata or product-adjacent files could bypass scope gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Add adversarial tests for .koala/foo.json and evidence/random.md remaining rejected.

preMortem.scenario: Allowed transcript path skips delivery-check semantics.
preMortem.trigger: Scope artifact classification is confused with DONE gate satisfaction.
preMortem.consequence: A story might appear deliverable without signed delivery-check evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep done-oracle untouched and add tests/docs stating classification is provenance only.

preMortem.scenario: Reviewer rebind still happens after transcript-only evidence.
preMortem.trigger: The transcript path changes scope-contract or review binding inputs rather than being classified as lifecycle artifact.
preMortem.consequence: The original B-bffc friction remains despite path allowlist.
preMortem.mitigation: Add a regression around scope_contract_check/review freshness for transcript-only diff.
